page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, running on an Intel Xeon 8559C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (tile and int8), and Total Memory Encryption (TME) for hardware-level security. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

For local storage, the i7i.xlarge bundles a 937 GB NVMe SSD, making it suitable for I/O-intensive operations. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is relatively weaker, as evidenced by bottom-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and clang software compilation. Memory read bandwidth also falls into the lower performance tier, though write bandwidth and database operations remain in the average range.

Given its high ratio of DDR5 memory to vCPUs and integrated high-speed NVMe SSD storage, the i7i.xlarge offers a resource-dense profile for storage-heavy workloads without requiring high vCPU counts. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads that are constrained by storage I/O and memory capacity rather than raw multi-core compute power. Appropriate workloads include relational and non-relational databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded data compression tasks.
